description:
FILED s473t5c (#1501 round 4), found by the #1681 probe set.  PRE-EXISTING and
`&`-free: identical on main 17d831fe and on the s473t5c tree, so #1681 neither
caused nor cured it.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):

    my $x = 1; my $y = 2;
    my $e = \($x, $y);
    print "SCALAR-CTX kind=", ref($e), " is_y=", ($e == \$y ? 1 : 0), "\n";
    my @a = \($x, $y);
    print "LIST-CTX n=", scalar(@a), " kinds=", join(",", map { ref } @a), "\n";

    perl:  SCALAR-CTX kind=SCALAR is_y=1     LIST-CTX n=2 kinds=SCALAR,SCALAR
    PCL :  SCALAR-CTX kind=ARRAY  is_y=0     LIST-CTX n=2 kinds=SCALAR,SCALAR

So the LIST context is right and the SCALAR one is not: perl's `\(LIST)` is a
list operator whose scalar-context value is the comma operator's, i.e. a
reference to the LAST element.

CAUSE, READ FROM THE CODE (not guessed).  `Pl::ExprToCL::gen_prefix_op_form`'s
`\(LIST)` branch has three sub-paths and only ONE of them applies the rule:

  * the general list path ends
        if (defined $raw_ctx && ($raw_ctx == SCALAR_CTX || $raw_ctx == VOID_CTX)) {
          return ['p-list-scalar', ['p-refgen-list', $list_form]];
        }
    -- correct, and its own comment says why;
  * `_gen_backslash_multi_term_form` (the `@$tv_kids > 1` path, which is the
    one a plain `\($x, $y)` takes) returns `['vector', …]` or the
    `let`+`p-vector-append` shape with NO context test at all -- that is the
    bug;
  * the single-child path is unaffected (`\($x)` is `\$x`).

FIX SHAPE: read `get_node_context_raw($node_id)` in the multi-term path the
way the general path does and wrap in `p-list-scalar` for SCALAR_CTX /
VOID_CTX.  The two paths asking the same question in two places is rule 11's
smell; the ceiling would be one helper both call.

ACCEPTANCE (probe vs perl 5.40.3): scalar and list context of `\($x, $y)`,
`\(&foo, &bar)` (ref to \&bar -- measured, `$e == \&bar` is 1), a range mix
`\($x, 1..2)` and a slice mix `\($x, @a[0,1])` in BOTH contexts, plus VOID
context (`\($x, $y);` as a statement) which must not change what runs.  The
guard file `Pl/t/backslash-amp-01.t` is the place for the rows.
subject: `\(A, B)` in SCALAR context answers an ARRAY ref where perl answers a ref to the LAST element (the comma operator) -- the multi-term `\(LIST)` path never gets the `p-list-scalar` wrap its sibling has
